ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a wind tunnel laboratory, wind with adjustable speed in the horizontal direction can be generated to study the forces acting on objects in a flowing gas. The principle of an instrument used to measure the wind force is shown in the figure. A slender, lightweight metal wire is fixed at one end to a suspension point $O$. The other end of the wire hangs a metal ball with a mass $m = 40\,\mathrm{g}$. When there is no wind, the metal wire hangs vertically downward. When wind blows horizontally at a speed $v = 10\,\mathrm{m/s}$, the metal wire deviates from the vertical direction by an angle $\theta$. The relationship between the wind force and the wind speed is given by $F = kv^{2}$, where $k = 3 \times 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{N \cdot s^{2}/m^{2}}$. Friction is negligible, and the gravitational acceleration is $g = 10\,\mathrm{m/s^{2}}$.

1. Find the magnitude of the tension force exerted by the metal sphere on the metal wire.
2. Find the numerical value of the deflection angle $\theta$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the upper part of the figure there is a suspension point O, a vertical reference line goes downward from O, and a metal wire connects from O obliquely to the lower left to a small ball; the angle θ between the metal wire and the vertical direction is marked. On the right side it is labeled wind, and a horizontal wind is drawn, indicating that the small ball deviates from the vertical direction under the action of a horizontal wind force. Reasoning calculation: According to the relation given in the problem, the magnitude of the wind force F = kv^2 = 3×10^-3×10^2 = 0.3 N. The mass of the small ball m = 40 g = 0.04 kg, therefore the gravity mg = 0.04×10 = 0.4 N. When the small ball is in static equilibrium, the tension of the metal wire is along the direction of the metal wire, and its components satisfy T sinθ = F, T cosθ = mg. So T = sqrt(F^2 + (mg)^2) = sqrt(0.3^2 + 0.4^2) = sqrt(0.25) = 0.5 N. Also tanθ = F/(mg) = 0.3/0.4 = 0.75, therefore θ ≈ arctan(0.75) ≈ 37°. The magnitude of the pulling force of the metal ball on the metal wire is equal to the magnitude of the tension of the metal wire on the ball.
